queue.title: Supplier Due Diligence: ESG Criteria
queue.content:
ESG assessment reduced to a questionnaire without on-site verification gives false security, not real risk insight. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

ESG supplier assessment reduced to a questionnaire without on-site verification gives a false sense of security, not a real picture of risk.

ESG supplier assessment reduced to a questionnaire without on-site verification gives a false sense of security, not a real picture of risk.

Regulatory pressure and demands from large business partners increasingly force companies to document ESG practice not just for their own operations, but across their entire supplier chain.

A standard ESG questionnaire filled out by a supplier, without independent verification or a site visit, easily becomes a formality that doesn't reflect actual practice on the ground.

Concentration risk grows when ESG assessment happens once at contract signing rather than periodically — supplier practice changes, and documentation often lags behind reality.

Companies that integrate ESG due diligence into regular supplier-management processes, rather than treating it as a separate compliance task, get a more accurate picture of real risk.

Cjelovit tekst i izvor: https://gnk-asg.hr/en/publications/supplier-due-diligence-esg-criteria/

queue.title: Renewable Energy: Corporate Contracts
queue.content:
A long-term renewable energy contract stabilises cost only if pricing mechanisms are correctly structured. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

A long-term renewable energy purchase agreement stabilises a company's energy cost, but only if the pricing mechanisms are correctly structured.

A long-term renewable energy purchase agreement stabilises a company's energy cost, but only if the pricing mechanisms are correctly structured.

A Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) lets a company lock in a renewable energy price 10 to 15 years in advance, protecting it from wholesale energy market volatility.

The contract structure — fixed price versus one tied to a market index, virtual versus physical PPA — determines the actual level of risk protection, and the differences are often underestimated in initial negotiations.

Companies that view a PPA purely through a sustainability lens, without detailed financial analysis of the pricing mechanism, may take on more market risk than intended.

Transparent reporting on energy origin from PPA contracts is increasingly becoming a condition for participating in public tenders and in large business partners' ESG reporting.

queue.title: Cross-Border Data Transfer Compliance
queue.content:
Cross-border data transfer needs a legal basis that changes faster than most companies' documentation. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

Cross-border data transfer requires a legal basis that changes faster than the average company's internal documentation.

Cross-border data transfer requires a legal basis that changes faster than the average company's internal documentation.

Companies operating in multiple countries routinely transfer personal and business data across borders, often without formally verifying whether the legal basis for that transfer is still valid.

Changes in a country's regulatory status can retroactively undermine transfer mechanisms that were previously fully compliant, without the company noticing until an audit is conducted.

A practical approach includes mapping all cross-border data flows, naming a person responsible for tracking regulatory changes, and contract clauses enabling quick adjustment of the transfer mechanism.

The cost of a one-time compliance review is almost always lower than the cost of a business disruption if a regulator later determines a data transfer lacked a valid legal basis.

Cjelovit tekst i izvor: https://gnk-asg.hr/en/publications/cross-border-data-transfer-compliance/
